simple.meaning: נְטַל (nᵉṭal) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to raise.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 4:31. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נְטַל (H5191) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: נְטַל (nᵉṭal) / H5191 is traced through Daniel 4:31, Daniel 7:4 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: While the word was in the king’s mouth, a voice came from the sky, saying, “O king Nebuchadnezzar, to you it is spoken: ‘The kingdom has departed from you.

timeline.evidenceText: While the word was in the king’s mouth, a voice came from the sky, saying, “O king Nebuchadnezzar, to you it is spoken: ‘The kingdom has departed from you.
“The first was like a lion, and had eagle’s wings. I watched until its wings were plucked, and it was lifted up from the earth, and made to stand on two feet as a man. A man’s heart was given to it.
